fc904_conflict_resolution.verdict: NO genuine conflict - the two requirements coincide
fc904_conflict_resolution.reasoning_frozen_before_implementation: FC-904 requests the DEFAULT role tuple, which names all five roles. The new request-scoped rule produces requested roles + ancestors, which for the full tuple is still all five. The assertion read == [] and produced == sorted(ALL_ROLES) therefore holds UNEDITED. The reviewer's counterexample was a SUBSET request, which the old code got wrong in both directions (summary-only returned an unrequested downstream dependent and omitted its ancestor; normalized-only returned all five).
fc904_conflict_resolution.residual_semantic_shift_recorded_not_hid: the JUSTIFICATION changes: pre-fix the result was independent of `roles` (a global produce-everything constant); post-fix it is a function of `roles`. The FC-904 assertions cannot distinguish the two, which is exactly why the subset counterexample was the finding that caught it. Documented in oracle.md (D1a), decision.md (D1a) and in the test test_no_bundle_default_request_is_universe_scope.
fc904_conflict_resolution.what_would_have_been_a_real_conflict: narrowing the default roles tuple to the 4 active-DAG roles would drop compatibility-only markdown and turn test_no_bundle_all_produced RED. That option was rejected in advance (decision.md D1 alternative 2) because it breaks a frozen acceptance test to fix a bug that does not require breaking it.
